name: Eli Lilly and Company

profile.description: Eli Lilly and Company discovers, develops, manufactures, and markets human pharmaceuticals worldwide, anchored by its incretin franchise — Mounjaro (tirzepatide for type 2 diabetes) and Zepbound (tirzepatide for obesity). Q3 2026 revenue rose 39% to $24.4B on 53% volume growth, with worldwide Mounjaro revenue up 65% to $10.7B, and management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $91-92B from $85-87B. FY2025 revenue was $65.2B with $20.6B of net income. Headquartered in Indianapolis and led by CEO David Ricks; market cap roughly $1.26T.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (3/3): Lilly converted decades of incretin research into Mounjaro and Zepbound, taking revenue from $24.5B in 2020 to $65.2B in 2025 and to a raised $91-92B 2026 guide; worldwide Mounjaro alone did $10.7B in Q3 2026 (+65%) [1][3]. AI Deployment (1/2): Lilly launched TuneLab, giving biotech companies access to Lilly-trained drug-discovery models, and announced a co-innovation AI lab in early 2026; CEO Ricks targets halving development timelines, but no quantified AI savings or AI revenue are disclosed [2]. Market Share (2/2): Q3 2026 volume grew 53% and Mounjaro/Zepbound exceeded half of 2025 revenue, making Lilly the incretin category leader and fastest share gainer [1][2]. Product Pipeline (2/2): Lilly is adding named assets through the AtaiBeckley and Curevo acquisitions ($4.2B acquired IPR&D in Q3 2026) on top of next-generation incretins, with revenue visibility embedded in a guidance raise of $5.5B [1]. R&D Intensity (1/1): FY2025 R&D of $13.3B equals 20.5% of revenue, top quartile for large-cap pharma [3].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): Lilly's purpose — uniting caring with discovery to create medicines that make life better for people around the world — is specific and traceable to strategic decisions such as heavy capacity investment and pipeline acquisitions, earning 3 rather than 4 because the GLP-1 era is recent and the mission has not been tested by an existential crisis [2]. Community Impact (1/2): Lilly runs long-standing corporate philanthropy through the Lilly Foundation and patient access programs, and ESG coverage highlights affordable access as a key managed risk, but our searches did not surface dollar-quantified, distinctive programs for this screen [5]. Employee Retention (0/2): No voluntary turnover or tenure data was found; headcount has grown to roughly 50,000 [4]. Insider Buying (0/2): No meaningful open-market insider purchases by executives were identified in the last 12 months.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Growth stock (10 weight units). D/E 122.9% scores 0.77 (1x) [4]. ROE 86.0% exceeds the 15% target, 1.0 (2x) [4]. Revenue growth YoY 38.6% scores 1.0 (1x) [4]. Revenue 5yr CAGR 21.6% (derived from FMP revenue of $24.54B in FY2020 to $65.18B in FY2025) scores 1.0 (2x) [3]. Forward P/E 28.13 scores 0.80 (1x) [4]. Profit margin 31.9% scores 1.0 (1x) [4]. PEG 1.36 (Yahoo Finance) scores 0.82 (2x) [4]. Weighted sum = 0.77 + 2.0 + 1.0 + 2.0 + 0.80 + 1.0 + 1.64 = 9.21 / 10 → 9. Liquidity floor passes easily: 2.57M shares × $1,410.99 ≈ $3.6B per day. EPS 5yr CAGR of 28.8% is derived from FMP diluted EPS ($6.47 → $22.95).

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Lilly's earnings rest on patented molecules, FDA-regulated clinical development, and physical manufacturing of injectables and orals — none of which AI can substitute; our search found no 2026 analyst source treating AI as a material risk to Lilly, and the company's own risk disclosures center on manufacturing, supply and regulatory actions [2]. The main AI-related risk is indirect: AI-accelerated discovery could shorten rivals' path to competing incretins, which keeps this at 8 rather than 9. AI Opportunity (0/1): Lilly is deploying AI (TuneLab models offered to biotechs, a 2026 AI co-innovation lab, Ricks' goal of halving development timelines), but it reports no quantifiable AI revenue, so the tiebreaker point is not awarded [2].

infinite_game.summary: Through Sinek's lens Lilly is a 150-year infinite player: its cause of making medicines that make life better has survived generations of leadership, patent cliffs, and industry consolidation, and the incretin franchise is the payoff of research begun long before obesity drugs were fashionable. Leadership keeps reinvesting at scale — $13.3B in R&D and $4.2B of pipeline acquisitions in a single quarter — rather than harvesting the windfall. The one gap is trust evidence: headcount has surged to ~50,000 and there is no hard retention data.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (3/3): 'Unite caring with discovery to create medicines that make life better' has guided Lilly from insulin to today's incretin franchise, enduring leadership transitions and patent cliffs; the cause is service-oriented and never fully achievable [2]. Strategic choices trace back to it — Q3 2026 volume up 53% even as realized prices fell 15%, indicating access is being prioritized alongside profit [1].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Ricks treats HR as a partner in defining culture, prizes curiosity and a 'best athlete' agility mindset, and has led since 2017, providing continuity [2]. However, rapid growth to roughly 50,000 employees and the absence of published turnover or tenure data prevent a high-trust score [4].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (1/1): Ricks' public framing centers on curiosity and asking better questions rather than destroying competitors, and Lilly shares Lilly-trained AI models with outside biotechs through TuneLab — behavior consistent with improving the field rather than only winning share [2].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (2/2): Lilly has reinvented itself from a diversified mid-tier pharma whose revenue was flat around $28B in 2021-2022 into the incretin leader guiding to $91-92B in 2026, reorganizing manufacturing, capital allocation and pipeline strategy around the shift [1][3]. Opening its discovery models to outside biotechs via TuneLab shows continued willingness to change its R&D model [2].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (2/2): Leadership absorbed $4.2B of acquired IPR&D charges in Q3 2026 (AtaiBeckley, Curevo), choosing to let the charges more than offset a $4.07 underlying EPS raise in order to build the next pipeline [1]. Lilly sustains R&D at 20.5% of revenue ($13.3B) and Ricks openly frames AI as a disruption to embrace rather than defend against [2][3].

investment_thesis: Eli Lilly at $1,410.99 is compounding at a pace without precedent for a trillion-dollar pharmaceutical company: Q3 2026 revenue grew 39% to $24.4B on 53% volume growth, Mounjaro reached $10.7B in a single quarter (+65%), and full-year 2026 revenue guidance was lifted by $5.5B at the midpoint to $91-92B [1]. Revenue has compounded at a 21.6% CAGR from $24.5B in 2020 to $65.2B in 2025, while net income more than tripled to $20.6B [3]. Profitability is elite — 31.9% net margin, 86% ROE, 53.7% operating margin — and the stock trades at 28.1x forward earnings with a 1.36 PEG, cheaper on a forward basis than many lower-growth peers [4]. R&D of $13.3B (20.5% of revenue) and continued pipeline buying (AtaiBeckley, Curevo) keep the next wave of medicines funded [1][3].
thesis_continued: The bear case is concentration and price. Mounjaro and Zepbound accounted for more than half of 2025 revenue, and Lilly's own filings flag manufacturing difficulties, third-party performance and supply disruptions as risks to product supply [2]. Realized prices fell 15% in Q3 2026 — volume is carrying growth while pricing erodes — and Q3 revenue included roughly $900M of one-time benefits (Jardiance milestones and rebate adjustments) that will not recur [1]. Acquired IPR&D charges of $4.2B in Q3 more than offset the underlying EPS raise, leaving adjusted 2026 EPS guidance at $35-36 [1]. D/E of 123% ($49.5B total debt vs $4.9B cash) reflects debt-funded capacity expansion [4]. S&P Global has placed Lilly's ESG score under review pending a Media & Stakeholder Analysis controversy case, and the Inspire Impact Score of -49 (MISALIGNED, LGBT Activism) may limit allocation for faith-based mandates [5].
key_catalysts: Full-year 2026 revenue guidance raised to $91-92B (from $85-87B) after Q3 revenue of $24.4B (+39%), with 53% volume growth signaling GLP-1 demand still outrunning supply additions [1]
Pipeline conversion beyond tirzepatide — newly acquired AtaiBeckley and Curevo assets ($4.2B of Q3 IPR&D) plus next-generation incretins broaden the revenue base beyond Mounjaro/Zepbound [1]
AI-accelerated drug discovery through the TuneLab model platform for biotechs and the 2026 co-innovation AI lab could compress development timelines that CEO Ricks has said AI might cut in half [2]
key_risks: Pricing erosion: realized prices fell 15% in Q3 2026; continued government, payer and competitive pressure on GLP-1 pricing could turn volume growth into flat revenue growth [1]

Franchise concentration: Mounjaro and Zepbound exceeded half of 2025 revenue, so any safety signal, supply disruption, or manufacturing failure (risks flagged in Lilly's own annual report) would hit the $1.26T valuation disproportionately [2]

Earnings quality: ~$900M of one-time Q3 revenue benefits and $4.2B of acquired IPR&D charges make GAAP results lumpy, and serial pipeline acquisitions financed alongside $49.5B of debt raise leverage risk [1][4]
